postText:
One unresponsive downstream legacy lab service once choked our entire healthcare IT network. Gateway worker pools filled with hanging TCP connections, crashing unaffected triage APIs.

When downstream services stall, naive retry loops and unbounded queues turn minor latency spikes into catastrophic cascade failures.

Here is how we stabilized our edge gateway:

1. Distributed Token Bucket Limiting
Enforce tenant and route limits at the edge via Redis cluster. Drop or queue abusive bursts before worker threads allocate memory.

2. Circuit Breakers with Fallback Caches
Monitor rolling 10-second error and timeout rates. When failure crosses 50%, trip circuit OPEN immediately. Return cached read payloads or fast 503s instead of burning upstream socket pools.

3. Bulkhead Partitioning
Isolate gateway thread pools and HTTP client connection pools per downstream domain. A frozen archival PACS system must never starve critical pharmacy or triage routing.

Resilience is not hoping dependencies never fail. Resilience is building gateways that isolate blast radiuses automatically.

In your architecture, do you rely on adaptive concurrency limits at the edge, or strict static circuit breaker thresholds?
